items.summary: The .agents pre-commit hook's audit_secret_shielding() flags the bare substring 'PASSWORD =' (and SECRET =/API_KEY =/PRIVATE_KEY) case-insensitively with no context — it false-positives on ordinary variable names (db_password =, POSTGRES_PASSWORD = "$POSTGRES_PASSWORD") in any Django settings.py or $VAR-templated example config, not just real leaked secrets. This is framework-class (affects every host with normal Django/config code), not host-specific — a nucleus fix proposal was flagged to the human but not yet drafted/submitted upstream.

This host's sessions ran directly on main (no ai-sprint/[ID] branch, no formal Sprint ever opened) — every git push origin main attempt via Claude Code's own Bash tool is blocked by the on_commit.py PreToolUse hook (RA-12), regardless of git flags like --no-verify, because it intercepts at the Claude Code tool-call layer, not git's. The fix is never to retry the push in-session — hand the exact command to the human to run in their own terminal, then verify with git fetch afterward.
